close_reason: Added dispatch_single_call and dispatch_batch_of_sixteen criterion benches to surface the per-call tokio::task::spawn overhead in the dispatcher hot path. Compiled with NoopHandler that returns Ok immediately so the timing measures dispatcher overhead, not handler work. The actual replace-spawn-with-catch_unwind decision is filed as JMAP-wlip.36 ('human' labelled, P3) because it requires (a) adding futures-util to the AGENTS.md dep allowlist and (b) accepting the behavioural change where tokio::task::JoinError::is_cancelled() distinction collapses into the panic-only path.
description:
Path: crate-jmap-server/src/lib.rs:177 task::spawn(async move { handler.call(...).await }).await. For a batch of N method calls (typical max_calls = 16; RFC 8620 §3 default), the dispatcher pays N tokio::task::spawn allocations (~120 bytes per JoinHandle + future heap alloc) and N scheduler context switches. Since the JoinHandle is awaited immediately, only one method call runs at a time. The spawn is purely for panic isolation, as documented.

Impact at scale: a server handling 10k JMAP requests/sec at avg 4 calls each = 40k extra spawns/sec. On a tokio multi-threaded runtime this is measurable: tokio::task::spawn benches at ~200ns + alloc overhead per call on x86_64. Net: ~8ms of CPU per second of wall-clock, plus heap pressure. Not catastrophic, but visible in a flamegraph.

Cheaper alternative for panic isolation: std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe + FutureExt::catch_unwind from futures-util. Catches panic without spawn — saves the alloc and the scheduler hop, keeps panic_message_not_in_response semantics intact. Adds one dep (futures-util) which the workspace already pulls in transitively.

The new benches in benches/dispatcher.rs cover parse_request and resolve_args but NOT Dispatcher::dispatch, so the spawn overhead is currently invisible in the regression baseline. Adding bench_dispatcher_single_call and bench_dispatcher_batch_of_16 would surface the cost and gate the alternative.

Expected impact at scale: low for non-hot-path consumers (kith, stoa at current scale); meaningful for a high-throughput proxy or a multi-tenant Mailbox server. The change is non-breaking — Dispatcher::dispatch's external behaviour is identical.
title: Dispatcher::dispatch spawns a tokio task per method call but immediately awaits — heap allocations with no concurrency benefit
